question: In secretory diarrhoea, the diarrhoea characteristically persists even when the patient fasts, because the secretory drive is independent of luminal contents.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Actually, this statement is true. Secretory diarrhoea persists on fasting because the secretory stimulus (e.g., toxin, hormone) is independent of luminal contents. Osmotic diarrhoea, by contrast, resolves with fasting once the offending solute is removed.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Secretory diarrhoea (e.g., cholera toxin activating adenylyl cyclase, raising cAMP) continues regardless of oral intake — this is the hallmark distinguishing it from osmotic diarrhoea, which resolves with fasting.
